σεις σπονδὴν σίκερα Κυρίῳ. Καὶ τὸν ἀμνὸν τὸν δεύτερον ποιήσεις πρὸς ἑσπέραν, κατὰ τὴν θυσίαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ κατὰ τὴν σπονδὴν αὐτοῦ ποιήσεις εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας τῷ Κυρίῳ.» Συνίης οὖν ὅπως τῶν θυσιῶν τὴν ἀναφορὰν ταῖς ἑορταῖς ὅτι μάλιστα πρέπειν ὁ θεῖος ἡμῖν ἐν τούτοις διισχυρίζεται νόμος· Χρῆναι γὰρ οἶμαι πάντη τε καὶ πάντως εὐωδιάζειν ἡμᾶς ἐν αὐταῖς τῷ Θεῷ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ πολιτείας τοὺς τρόπους, οἱονεί πως ἐν τάξει ποιουμένους θυμιαμάτων, καὶ εὔοσμον ὁλοκαύτωμα προσκομίζοντας αὐτοὺς τῷ Θεῷ κατ' ἐκεῖνο, οἶμαί που, τὸ μάλα ὀρθῶς εἰρημένον· «Παραστήσατε οὖν τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν θυσίαν ζῶσαν ἁγίαν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ὑμῶν.» Τὴν δέ γε τοῦ ἐνδελεχισμοῦ θυσίαν ἀποπεραίνεσθαι δεῖν εὖ μάλα φησὶν, ἑνὸς μὲν ἀμνοῦ σφαζομένου τὸ πρωῒ, ἑτέρου δὲ αὖ πρὸς ἑσπέραν, συνθυμιωμένης αὐτοῖς σεμιδάλεως, ἐλαίου τε καὶ οἴνου προσεπενηνεγμένων· ἐν παντὶ γὰρ καιρῷ καὶ ἀκαταλήκτως καὶ ἀπαρχῆς μέχρι τέλους ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ, τουτέστιν, ἐν Ἐκκλησίᾳ, διὰ πάσης ἀρετῆς εὐωδιάζομεν ἐν Χριστῷ. Τὸ γὰρ πρωΐ τε καὶ πρὸς ἑσπέραν καπνίζεσθαι τοὺς ἀμνοὺς, ὑποτύπωσις ἂν εἴη πάλιν, τοῦ δι' ἡμᾶς τε καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἀναθρώσκοντος τῷ Πατρὶ, συνανακομίζοντος δὲ ὥσπερ αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν τῶν εἰς αὐτὸν πιστευσάντων ζωὴν, τὸ ἱλαρὸν ἔχουσαν ὡς ἐν ἐλπίδι βεβαίας δόξης τε καὶ βασιλείας. Καὶ πρός γε δὴ τούτῳ, τὸ κατευφραίνεσθαι δεῖν, ταῖς εἰς αἰῶνα τρυφαῖς· σημεῖον δ' ἂν γένοιτο τῆς τοιᾶσδε ζωῆς, σεμίδαλις ἐλαιόδευτος, καὶ οἰνοβραχής. Θυσία δὴ οὖν σωτηρίου τὸ χρῆμα, καθὰ καὶ ἡ τετελεσμένη διὰ Μωσέως ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ. Γέγραπται δὲ ἐν τῇ Ἐξόδῳ, ὅτε τοὺς ἐφ' ἅπασι τοῖς πρακτέοις διωρίσατο νόμους τοῦ πάντων κρατοῦντος Θεοῦ· «Ὀρθρίσας,» φησὶν, «ὁ Μωσῆς τὸ πρωῒ ᾠκοδόμησε θυσιαστήριον ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος, καὶ δώδεκα λίθους εἰς τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ· καὶ ἐξαπέστειλε τοὺς νεανίσκους τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἀνήνεγκαν ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ θυσίαν σωτηρίου τῷ Θεῷ, μοσχάρια.» Ἀδιαφορήσει δὲ, οἶμαι, τῆς θυσίας ὁ λόγος, εἴτ' οὖν ἀμνοὶ τὰ ἱερουργούμενα, κἂν εἴτε μοσχάρια λέγοιντο τυχόν· σώζεται γὰρ ἐν ἀμφοῖν τῆς ἀκακίας ὁ τύπος, ὃ δὴ μάλιστα περιθείη τις ἂν τῷ προσώπῳ Χριστοῦ, διὰ φωνῆς Ἱερεμίου λέγοντος· «Ἐγὼ δὲὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον, ἀγόμενον τοῦ θύεσθαι οὐκ ἔγνων.» Εἰ δὲ δή τις ἕλοιτο καὶ καθ' ἕτερον τρόπον, πρωϊνήν τε καὶ ἑσπερινὴν θυσίαν ἐπινενοῆσθαι λέγειν ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ διά τοι τὸν τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος χρόνον, εἶναι μὲν εὐώδη, πρὸ τῆς παραβάσεως τῆς ἐν Ἀδὰμ, τοιουτονὶ δὲ γενέσθαι πάλιν τὸν ἐν ἐσχάτοις καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ, καὶ ἐν τῇ κατ' αὐτὸν νοουμένῃ ζωῇ, φέροιτο οὐκ ἂν ἀπὸ σκοποῦ, καὶ λογιεῖται σοφῶς· ἔχει γὰρ ὧδε τὸ χρῆμα τῇ φύσει.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Πείθομαι.
{ΚΥΡ.} Τὰς δὲ ἐν τῷ Σαββάτῳ θυσίας ὁρίζεται λέγων εὐθύς· «Καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν Σαββάτων προσάξετε δύο ἀμνοὺς ἐνιαυσίους ἀμώμους, καὶ δύο δέκατα σεμιδάλεως ἀναπεποιημένης ἐν ἐλαίῳ εἰς θυσίαν καὶ
pass_a_gloss: (you will pour) a libation of strong drink to the Lord. And the second lamb you will do toward evening, according to its sacrifice and according to its libation you will do for an odor of fragrance to the Lord.' Do you understand then how the divine law insists to us in these things that the offering-up of the sacrifices befits the feasts most of all? For it is needful, I think, wholly and in every way that we in them make fragrant to God the ways of the citizenship in Christ, as it were making them in the order of incenses, and bringing ourselves to God as a sweet-smelling whole burnt offering according to that, I think, which was very rightly said: 'Present then your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, well-pleasing to God, your reasonable worship.' And the sacrifice of continuance he says very well must be completed, one lamb slaughtered in the morning, and another again toward evening, fine flour burned with them, both oil and wine brought in addition; for in every season and unceasingly and from beginning to end in the holy tent, that is, in the Church, we are fragrant through every virtue in Christ. For the lambs being burned in the morning and toward evening would again be an outline of the one who for us and on our behalf leaps up for an odor of fragrance to the Father, and carries up with him as it were also the life of those who believed in him, having cheerfulness as in hope of sure glory and kingdom. And in addition to this, that one must rejoice in the delights unto the age; and a sign of such life would be fine flour oil-moistened and wine-soaked. A sacrifice then of salvation is the thing, as also the one performed through Moses on mount Sinai. And it is written in Exodus, when he determined the laws of the God ruling all about all things to be done: 'Rising early', he says, 'Moses in the morning built an altar on the mountain, and twelve stones for the twelve tribes of Israel; and he sent out the young men of the sons of Israel, and they offered up whole burnt offerings and a sacrifice of salvation to God, calves.' And the account of the sacrifice will make no difference, I think, whether then lambs are the things sacrificed, or whether they should perhaps be called calves; for in both the type of innocence is preserved, which one would put especially on the person of Christ, saying through the voice of Jeremiah: 'But I as an innocent lamb, led to be sacrificed, did not know.' And if someone should choose also in another way to say that the morning and evening sacrifice in the holy tent was devised on account of the time of humanity, to be fragrant before the transgression in Adam, and such to become again in the last times and in Christ, and in the life understood according to him, he would not go away from the mark, and will reason wisely; for thus the thing holds by nature. PALL.: I am persuaded. CYR.: And the sacrifices on the Sabbath he defines saying at once: 'And on the day of the Sabbaths you will bring two lambs a year old unblemished, and two tenths of fine flour mixed in oil for a sacrifice and (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …a drink offering of strong drink to the Lord. And the second lamb you shall offer toward evening; according to its sacrifice and according to its drink offering you shall offer it, for a fragrant aroma to the Lord’ (Numbers 28:7–8). Do you understand, then, how the divine law insists to us here that the offering up of sacrifices is most fitting at the feasts? For I think we must at them, wholly and in every way, make the ways of the life in Christ give off a fragrance to God, presenting them as if in the rank of incense, and bringing ourselves to God as a fragrant whole burnt offering, according, I think, to the saying that is so rightly spoken: ‘Present your bodies, then, as a living sacrifice, holy, well pleasing to God, which is your reasonable service’ (Romans 12:1).

He says, very well, that the continual sacrifice must be completed with one lamb slaughtered in the morning and another toward evening, with fine flour burned together with them, and oil and wine brought in addition. For at every time, without ceasing, from beginning to end, in the holy tent, that is, in the Church, we give off a fragrance in Christ through every virtue. The burning of the lambs in the morning and toward evening would be, again, an outline of him who for us and on our behalf rises up to the Father as a fragrant aroma, and carries up with him, as it were, the life of those who have believed in him, a life that is cheerful, as resting in the hope of sure glory and kingdom. And besides this it shows that we must rejoice in the delights that last forever; and a sign of such a life would be fine flour moistened with oil and soaked in wine.

So the thing is a sacrifice of salvation, like the one Moses performed on Mount Sinai. It is written in Exodus, when he had laid down the laws of God, who rules all things, on everything that was to be done: ‘Rising early in the morning,’ it says, ‘Moses built an altar on the mountain, and twelve stones for the twelve tribes of Israel; and he sent the young men of the sons of Israel, and they offered whole burnt offerings and a sacrifice of salvation to God, calves’ (Exodus 24:4–5). The meaning of the sacrifice will make no difference, I think, whether the victims are lambs or whether perhaps they are called calves. For in both the type of innocence is kept, and one would apply it above all to the person of Christ, who says through the voice of Jeremiah, ‘But I was like an innocent lamb led to be slaughtered, and I did not know’ (Jeremiah 11:19). And if someone should choose to say, in another way, that the morning and evening sacrifice in the holy tent was conceived with a view to the time of mankind, that it was fragrant before the transgression in Adam, and that it became so again in the last times and in Christ, and in the life understood in him, he would not be wide of the mark, and his reasoning would be wise; for that is how the matter stands by its nature.

Cyril's text; the Greek Bible of Exodus 24:4 reads 'under the mountain'.
The verb 'pour' was rendered at the end of §26; the rest of the clause here.
